question: In the operation theatre, a surgeon removes an amputated limb (human anatomical waste). After the procedure, soiled dressings, used rubber gloves, and the amputated limb are present. Which correctly matches each waste item to its BMW Rules 2016 disposal container?

answers.text: Amputated limb → Yellow bag; soiled dressings → Yellow bag; used gloves → Red bag

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Under BMW Rules 2016: human anatomical waste (Category 1) → yellow bag for incineration or deep burial; soiled linen/dressings (Category 2) → yellow bag; contaminated recyclables such as gloves (Category 3) → red bag for autoclaving before recycling.

answers.text: Amputated limb → Red bag; soiled dressings → Yellow bag; used gloves → Blue container

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Amputated limbs are human anatomical waste (Category 1) and must go into yellow bags, not red. Red bags are for contaminated recyclable waste. Blue containers are for glass/metallic items.

answers.text: Amputated limb → Yellow bag; soiled dressings → Red bag; used gloves → White container

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Soiled dressings are Category 2 waste → yellow bag (not red). White translucent containers are reserved for sharps (Category 10), not gloves.

answers.text: Amputated limb → Black bag; soiled dressings → Red bag; used gloves → Yellow bag

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Black bags are for general solid waste. Human anatomical waste must always go to yellow bags for high-temperature incineration or deep burial — never to black/general waste bags.

overallFeedback.feedback: Revisit the BMW Rules 2016 colour-code system: yellow for anatomical/infectious/pharmaceutical waste, red for contaminated recyclables, white for sharps, blue for glass/metallic items.
Excellent application. Remembering the triad — anatomical waste → yellow, recyclable contaminated → red, sharps → white — is the clinical segregation rule under BMW Rules 2016.
